framing: Uses 'safe / not-safe / uh-oh' (not 'good/bad touch'); correct body-part names (AAP); the PANTS backbone; empower-not-frighten; it's never your fault; gender-neutral (POCSO).

categories.my-body: My body belongs to me (body autonomy)
categories.real-names: Real names for body parts; private parts
categories.safe-unsafe: Safe / not-safe / uh-oh touch (the uh-oh feeling)
categories.consent: Say no, even to family; ask first; change your mind
categories.tell: Tell a trusted adult; safety team; never your fault

evidenceBase: Safe/unsafe + 'uh-oh feeling'; secrets vs surprises; trusted-adult network

scenarios.situation: Lensy asks: whose body is your body?
scenarios.prompt: Who is the boss of your body?
scenarios.relearn: Your body belongs to you. You're the boss of it.
scenarios.myth: Grown-ups are the boss of your body.
scenarios.source: NSPCC PANTS (your body belongs to you)

scenarios.situation: An auntie pinches your cheeks hard and you don't like it.
scenarios.prompt: Can you say you don't like it?
scenarios.relearn: You can say 'please stop, I don't like that', even to family.
scenarios.source: PANTS (no means no, even to family)

scenarios.situation: Your cousin wants to wrestle but you're done playing.
scenarios.relearn: You decide what happens to your body. 'Stop' is enough.

scenarios.situation: Someone says 'give me a kiss or you're not a good kid'.
scenarios.relearn: Being a good kid never means doing things with your body you don't want.
scenarios.myth: Good kids must hug and kiss when told.

scenarios.situation: You want to sit a little apart from a hug-y relative.
scenarios.relearn: Wanting your own space is okay and not rude.

scenarios.situation: A friend grabs your hand to pull you along.
scenarios.prompt: Can you ask them to let go?
scenarios.relearn: You can ask anyone to stop touching you.

scenarios.situation: Boys and girls both wonder if these rules are for them.
scenarios.relearn: Body safety is for every child, boys and girls alike.
scenarios.myth: Body safety is only a girls' thing.

scenarios.situation: You feel proud saying 'my body, my rules'.
scenarios.relearn: That's the whole idea. Your body, your rules.

scenarios.situation: Someone bigger says 'do what I say, I'm older'.
scenarios.prompt: Does older mean boss of your body?
scenarios.relearn: Being older doesn't make someone the boss of your body.
scenarios.myth: Older people decide about your body.

scenarios.situation: You don't want your photo taken in the bath.
scenarios.relearn: No photos of your private parts, ever. You can say no.

scenarios.situation: A toy is shared, but your body is not a toy.
scenarios.prompt: Is your body something to share when asked?
options: No, my body is only mine
scenarios.answer: No, my body is only mine
scenarios.relearn: Toys can be shared. Your body is only yours.

scenarios.situation: You change your mind about a piggyback ride.
scenarios.relearn: You can change your mind about your body anytime.

scenarios.situation: Lensy points at an elbow.
scenarios.relearn: Every body part has a real name. Knowing them is smart.

scenarios.situation: There are parts a swimsuit covers.
scenarios.prompt: Do private parts have real names too?
scenarios.relearn: Private parts have real names and naming them is never rude.
scenarios.myth: Private parts are rude to name.

scenarios.situation: A grown-up uses a calm, real name for a body part.
scenarios.prompt: Is it okay for body parts to have real names like 'penis' or 'vulva'?
scenarios.relearn: Real names, said calmly, are normal and help keep you safe.

scenarios.situation: You knew the real name and could tell the doctor where it hurt.
scenarios.relearn: Real names let you explain anything clearly, a rash or a worry.

scenarios.situation: A kid giggles at the word for a private part.
scenarios.prompt: Is the word a joke or just a name?
scenarios.relearn: It's just a real name, like 'knee' or 'nose'. No shame.

scenarios.situation: Lensy names a nose, a knee, and an ear.
scenarios.relearn: We name all parts the same calm way.

scenarios.situation: Which parts are the 'private parts'?
scenarios.relearn: Private parts are the ones your underwear or swimsuit covers.

scenarios.situation: Someone says only girls should learn these names.
scenarios.prompt: Should all kids know the real names?
scenarios.relearn: Every child should know the real names for their body.
scenarios.myth: Only girls need to learn this.

scenarios.situation: You learned a new real name today.
scenarios.prompt: How do you feel knowing it?
scenarios.relearn: Knowing your body's names is a smart, safe thing.

scenarios.situation: A grown-up calls a private part by a silly nickname only.
scenarios.relearn: Silly names are fine for fun, but knowing the real one keeps you safe.

scenarios.situation: Grandma gives you a warm hug you like.
scenarios.relearn: A wanted hug is a safe touch; it feels good.

scenarios.situation: A high-five from a friend.
scenarios.relearn: High-fives are safe, happy touches.

scenarios.situation: Someone tries to touch the parts under your underwear.
scenarios.relearn: No one should touch your private parts. That's not safe; say no and tell.

scenarios.situation: A touch gives you a sweaty, fast-heart, icky feeling.
scenarios.prompt: What is that feeling telling you?
scenarios.relearn: That uh-oh feeling is your helper. Listen to it and tell someone.

scenarios.situation: A tickle that you're laughing at but want to stop now.
scenarios.relearn: Even a fun touch must stop when you say stop.

scenarios.situation: A doctor needs to check you and explains why, with a parent there.
options: Yes, with a parent and a reason
scenarios.answer: Yes, with a parent and a reason
scenarios.relearn: A doctor may check, but a trusted grown-up is there and it's explained. You can still ask why.
scenarios.source: PANTS (exceptions: health, with a trusted adult)

scenarios.situation: A pat on the back after you did well.
scenarios.relearn: A friendly pat on the back is a safe touch.

scenarios.situation: Someone hurts you on purpose.
scenarios.relearn: A touch that hurts on purpose is not safe. Tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: A touch you feel unsure about - not clearly safe, not clearly bad.
scenarios.prompt: What can you do with an unsure feeling?
scenarios.relearn: Even 'unsure' is worth telling a trusted adult about.

scenarios.situation: Helping hands at bath-time from your parent, to keep you clean.
scenarios.prompt: Is help with hygiene from a trusted carer okay?
scenarios.relearn: A trusted carer may help keep you clean; it's calm and explained, and you can speak up if unsure.

scenarios.situation: Your body feels goosebumpy and you want to move away from someone.
scenarios.relearn: Your body's warning is wise. Move to safety and tell.

scenarios.situation: A snuggle with someone you trust while reading a book.
scenarios.relearn: A wanted snuggle with someone you trust is safe and lovely.

scenarios.situation: Someone says 'this is our special touch, don't tell'.
scenarios.prompt: What does 'don't tell' about touch mean?
options: Tell a trusted adult right away
scenarios.answer: Tell a trusted adult right away
scenarios.relearn: 'Don't tell' about touch is a big warning. Tell a trusted adult.
scenarios.myth: If a touch is secret, keep it secret.

scenarios.situation: A handshake when you meet someone new.
scenarios.relearn: A handshake is a safe, friendly touch.

scenarios.situation: A 'not safe' touch happened. You did nothing wrong.
scenarios.prompt: Whose fault is an unsafe touch?
scenarios.relearn: If someone touches you unsafely, it is NEVER your fault.

scenarios.situation: You see a friend being touched in an unsafe way.
scenarios.relearn: Telling a trusted adult helps keep friends safe too.

scenarios.situation: PANTS rule P: Privates are private.
scenarios.prompt: Should anyone ask to see or touch your private parts?
scenarios.relearn: Privates are private. No one should ask to see or touch them.

scenarios.situation: PANTS rule A: Always remember your body belongs to you.
scenarios.relearn: Always: your body belongs to you.

scenarios.situation: PANTS rule N: No means no.
scenarios.prompt: If you say no, what does it mean?
scenarios.relearn: No means no, even to someone you love.

scenarios.situation: PANTS rule T: Talk about secrets that upset you.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with an upsetting secret?
scenarios.relearn: Talk about any secret that upsets you.

scenarios.situation: PANTS rule S: Speak up, someone can help.
scenarios.prompt: If something feels wrong, who can help?
scenarios.relearn: Speak up. Someone you trust can help, and will keep listening.

scenarios.situation: Someone wants to show you pictures of private parts.
scenarios.relearn: No one should show you pictures of private parts. Say no and tell.

scenarios.situation: A game asks you to take off your underwear.
scenarios.relearn: No game should ask about your private parts. Stop and tell.

scenarios.situation: You're at the beach in a swimsuit.
scenarios.prompt: Are the swimsuit parts the private parts?
scenarios.relearn: The parts a swimsuit covers are your private parts.

scenarios.situation: Someone asks you to keep a 'special game' about bodies a secret.
scenarios.prompt: What kind of secret is this?
scenarios.relearn: Body secrets you're told to keep are not okay. Tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: A boy wonders if PANTS is for him too.
scenarios.prompt: Is the underwear rule for boys too?
scenarios.relearn: PANTS is for every child, boys included.
scenarios.myth: The underwear rule is only for girls.

scenarios.situation: You want to remember the rule.
scenarios.prompt: Sing the PANTS idea with Lensy:
options: Private, Always-mine, No, Talk, Speak up
scenarios.answer: Private, Always-mine, No, Talk, Speak up
scenarios.relearn: P-A-N-T-S: a little song to remember staying safe.

scenarios.situation: A trusted carer helps with a hurt in a private area, calmly and explained.
scenarios.prompt: Is a health reason an exception?
options: Yes, with a trusted adult and a reason
scenarios.answer: Yes, with a trusted adult and a reason
scenarios.relearn: Health and hygiene are exceptions, with a trusted adult and a clear reason; you can still ask why.

scenarios.situation: You're saying bye and don't want to hug an uncle.
scenarios.relearn: A wave or high-five is fine. You choose how to say bye.

scenarios.situation: Before hugging a friend, what's kind to do?
scenarios.relearn: Asking first is kind. Consent works both ways.

scenarios.situation: Your friend says 'no thanks' to a hug.
scenarios.relearn: When someone says no, we stop. That's respect.

scenarios.situation: You said yes to a tickle but now want it to stop.
scenarios.relearn: Yes can change to no. You can stop anytime.

scenarios.situation: A relative insists 'just one kiss for me'.
scenarios.relearn: You can say no to kisses, even to family who love you.
scenarios.myth: You must kiss family if they ask.

scenarios.situation: Your little sibling is grabbing your toy and your hand.
scenarios.prompt: Can you set a body boundary kindly?
scenarios.relearn: You can protect your body with kind words first.

scenarios.situation: A friend wants to hold hands and you're okay with that.
scenarios.relearn: Saying yes to a touch you like is okay. Consent is about your choice.

scenarios.situation: Someone tickles you fast before you can answer.
scenarios.relearn: Asking first gives you a real choice.

scenarios.situation: You don't want to sit on someone's lap.
scenarios.prompt: Can you choose where to sit?
scenarios.relearn: You can choose. 'I'll sit here instead' is fine.

scenarios.situation: A grown-up respects your no and smiles.
scenarios.prompt: How do safe grown-ups react to your no?
scenarios.relearn: Safe grown-ups respect your no. If someone won't, tell another trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: Your friend keeps hugging after you said stop.
options: Move away and tell a grown-up
scenarios.answer: Move away and tell a grown-up
scenarios.relearn: If 'stop' isn't respected, move away and tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: Two kids both want a turn at a hug-game and both say yes happily.
scenarios.relearn: When both people happily choose, that's good consent.

scenarios.situation: You feel pressured by 'everyone's doing it'.
scenarios.relearn: What others do doesn't decide for your body. You do.

scenarios.situation: You want a hug from someone you love.
scenarios.prompt: Can you ask for a safe touch you want?
scenarios.relearn: You can ask for hugs you want too. Your body, your choice.

scenarios.situation: A hidden birthday gift you'll give grandma on Sunday.
scenarios.relearn: A surprise is happy and gets told soon. That's okay.

scenarios.situation: Someone says 'keep this between us, don't ever tell, or you'll be in trouble'.
scenarios.relearn: A secret you must keep forever, with fear, is not okay. Tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: Planning a surprise party for mum next week.
scenarios.relearn: Surprises make people happy and are shared soon. Lovely.

scenarios.situation: A secret that makes your tummy feel icky.
scenarios.prompt: What does an icky-secret feeling mean?
scenarios.relearn: If a secret feels icky, that's your sign to tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: A grown-up says a touch must be 'our little secret'.
scenarios.relearn: Touch is never a secret. Tell a trusted adult straight away.
scenarios.myth: Touch secrets are okay to keep.

scenarios.situation: You forgot it was a surprise and almost told. Is that a disaster?
scenarios.prompt: Is it okay if a surprise slips out?
scenarios.relearn: Surprises are low-stakes; no fear attached. That's how you tell them apart.

scenarios.situation: A friend shares a worry and asks you not to tell anyone.
scenarios.prompt: What if it's about someone being unsafe?
options: Tell a trusted adult to help
scenarios.answer: Tell a trusted adult to help
scenarios.relearn: Some worries need a grown-up's help. Telling to keep someone safe is right.

scenarios.situation: You're told to lie about a touch.
scenarios.prompt: Should you lie to cover a touch?
options: No, tell the truth to a trusted adult
scenarios.answer: No, tell the truth to a trusted adult
scenarios.relearn: Never lie to cover a touch. The truth keeps you safe.

scenarios.situation: Who is on your safety team?
scenarios.relearn: Pick a few trusted grown-ups, your safety team, so there's always someone.

scenarios.situation: You told one grown-up but they didn't listen.
scenarios.relearn: If one grown-up doesn't help, keep telling until someone does.

scenarios.situation: Something unsafe happened. You feel it might be your fault.
scenarios.relearn: It is never, ever your fault. The grown-up who did it is responsible.

scenarios.situation: You're scared to tell because of a threat.
scenarios.prompt: Should a threat stop you telling?
scenarios.relearn: Threats are how unsafe people stay hidden. Telling a trusted adult is brave and right.

scenarios.situation: You don't know who to call for help in India.
scenarios.prompt: Is there a helpline for children?
scenarios.relearn: Childline 1098 is a free helpline for children, any time. A grown-up can help you call.

scenarios.situation: A teacher is on your safety team at school.
scenarios.prompt: Can a teacher be a trusted adult?
scenarios.relearn: Teachers and other safe grown-ups can be on your safety team too.

scenarios.situation: You told and the grown-up said 'thank you for telling me'.
scenarios.relearn: Telling is always right. Safe grown-ups are glad you told.

scenarios.situation: A boy is unsure if these safety rules and helplines are for him.
scenarios.prompt: Are safety and help for boys too?
scenarios.relearn: Safety, telling and helplines are for every child, boys included.
scenarios.myth: Boys don't get hurt this way / don't need help.

scenarios.situation: You want to practise what to say.
scenarios.relearn: A simple start: 'I need to tell you something.' Then say what happened.

scenarios.situation: You feel relief after telling a trusted adult.
scenarios.relearn: Telling often makes the heavy feeling lighter. You're not alone.

scenarios.situation: A friend tells you something unsafe happened to them.
options: Help them tell a trusted adult
scenarios.answer: Help them tell a trusted adult
scenarios.relearn: You can help a friend by going with them to a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: You're not sure if something counts as 'bad enough' to tell.
scenarios.prompt: Do you have to be sure before telling?
scenarios.relearn: You never need to be sure. If in doubt, tell a trusted adult.

scenarios.situation: Your safety-team grown-up gives you a hug after you told.
scenarios.relearn: Telling is one of the bravest things a kid can do.

scenarios.situation: Lensy reminds you of the whole idea.
options: I'm the boss, and I can always tell
I must do as I'm told
scenarios.answer: I'm the boss, and I can always tell
scenarios.relearn: My body, my rules: I'm the boss of my body, and I can always tell a trusted adult.
